body.statement: Fix \((p,k,m,M,s,V)\in\mathfrak T\), \(\pi_0\in(0,1/2)\), and \(G<\infty\). The image \(\Theta=\{\theta(P):P\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm{adm}}_{p,k}(m,M,s,V;\pi_0,G)\}\) is compact. For each fixed \(\nu_*>0\), the Wald-separated image \(\Theta_+(\nu_*)\) is a compact subset of \(\Theta\). The raw-moment map \(Q:\Theta\to Q(\Theta)\) is continuous and one-to-one with continuous inverse, every \(b_S\) with \(S\in\mathcal A\) is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(\Theta\), and \(\Omega:\Theta\to\mathbb S_+^{d_p}\) is continuous with \(\inf_{\vartheta\in\Theta}\min_{1\le j\le d_p}\Omega_{jj}(\vartheta)>0\).
body.justification: This proposition puts compactness, endpoint smoothness, and raw-moment covariance regularity in the finite-dimensional parameter space on which both inference procedures operate.
body.gap: These are standard finite-dimensional Gaussian moment facts used to specialize generic sample-split and projection inference; they are not part of the angular-frontier novelty claim.
body.consumer: The two inference theorems obtain a type-correct common domain and well-defined uniformity quantifiers.
